summary: First deep pass for GW5 now that waivers have processed and the 15-man squad is final. Twelve of fifteen look nailed or close to it; the two City men (Gvardiol, Haaland) were simply rested for tonight's Carabao Cup tie and are pencilled back in for Sunday, not doubts. The real uncertainty is at the back and in midfield where no permitted outlet has yet published this weekend's confirmed team news - Raya, Van Hecke, Ajayi, Scott and the three Bournemouth/Brentford mids are all treated as 'likely' rather than 'start' purely because that confirmation hasn't landed yet, not because of any actual fitness doubt.

players.name: Pickford
players.verdict: Undisputed No.1, no fresh fitness concern
players.note: Everton's own lineup pages have started Pickford in every league game this season, most recently the derby draw with Man Utd. No permitted outlet has yet published Saturday's confirmed team news for the Ipswich visit, but nothing has surfaced to put his place in doubt.

sources.title: Starting Lineups - Everton vs Man Utd

players.name: Raya
players.verdict: No fresh fitness concern; undisputed No.1
players.note: A search-engine claim of a Raya knee problem after the Man City game never traced back to arsenal.com or Sky Sports, and Arsenal's own site this week covers Saliba (out) and Timber's return, not Raya. No permitted outlet has yet published Saturday's confirmed team news for the trip to Brighton.

players.name: Bogle
players.verdict: Nailed at right-back, fresh off a goal and Player of the Match
players.note: Bogle scored and was named Newcastle's own Hisense Player of the Match in Monday's 4-1 win, and Daniel Farke's fitness update this week for Sunday's trip to Crystal Palace reports an almost fully fit squad with no mention of him as a doubt.

sources.title: Leeds United v Newcastle United match centre
Daniel Farke provides fitness update ahead of Crystal Palace clash

players.name: Vuskovic
players.verdict: Nailed teenage centre-back, just scored his first goal
players.note: Vuskovic scored his first Brighton goal in the recent draw with Leeds and Lewis Dunk praised his progress on the club's own site. No fitness concern has been reported ahead of Saturday's visit from Arsenal.

sources.title: Dunk's delight at progress of Vuskovic and Yalcouye

players.name: Ajayi
players.verdict: Fit and scoring in his last confirmed appearance
players.note: Sky Sports' own lineup for the 22 August win over Man Utd has Ajayi starting and scoring, but no permitted outlet has since published a line-up or press conference confirming him for this weekend's game against Newcastle, and unconfirmed reports of a hamstring complaint around that time were never verified on a permitted site.

sources.title: Starting Lineups - Hull City vs Man Utd

players.name: Van Hecke
players.note: Van Hecke has been a first-choice centre-back since his £52m move from Brighton and Tottenham's own coverage of him this week raises no fitness concern. No permitted outlet has yet published Saturday's confirmed team news for the visit of Aston Villa.

players.name: Gvardiol
players.verdict: Rested for tonight's Cup tie, pencilled in for Sunderland
players.note: Man City's own team news says Gvardiol, Haaland and Dias were left out entirely for tonight's Carabao Cup tie with Norwich purely as workload management after Sunday's derby, and describes it as 'highly unlikely' any of the three are risked in the cup - all three are expected back for Sunday's league game at home to Sunderland.

sources.title: Maresca provides injury update and team news ahead of Canaries clash

players.name: Barcola
players.verdict: Two straight starts, trending up not down
players.note: Barcola has started Liverpool's last two matches (the Atletico Madrid Champions League tie and the win over Fulham), and Alexander Isak publicly backed him this week to make the side 'much better as a team'. No permitted outlet has yet published a confirmed line-up for Sunday's trip to Bournemouth, but the trend clearly favours another start - the board's 0.26 availability is well behind where he actually is.

sources.title: Alexander Isak on his fitness and form, Liverpool fans and Barcola excitement

players.name: Lewis-Potter
players.verdict: No injury flagged; expected at wing-back vs Chelsea
players.note: Brentford's own preview for Friday's west London derby with Chelsea raises no fitness concern over Lewis-Potter. No permitted outlet has yet published the confirmed team sheet ahead of kick-off.

sources.title: Match previews: Brentford v Chelsea, Premier League, 18/09/2026

players.name: Scott
players.verdict: No injury reported; established Bournemouth starter
players.note: No permitted outlet has reported any fitness concern over Scott this week. No confirmed team news for Sunday's visit of Liverpool has been published yet, but nothing suggests his regular starting role is under threat.

players.name: Tavernier
players.verdict: Back from hamstring trouble and scoring again
players.note: Tavernier missed time earlier in the season with a hamstring injury but Sky Sports' own footage shows him back on the scoresheet against Man City since. No permitted outlet has yet confirmed his involvement specifically for Sunday's visit of Liverpool.

sources.title: Bournemouth: Marcus Tavernier scores against Man City

players.name: Schade
players.verdict: No injury flagged; expected to start vs Chelsea
players.note: Brentford's own preview for the Chelsea derby makes no mention of any fitness doubt over Schade. No permitted outlet has yet published Friday's confirmed team sheet.

sources.title: Match previews: Brentford v Chelsea, Premier League, 18/09/2026

players.name: Marmoush
players.verdict: Nailed first-choice striker, still without a league goal
players.note: De Zerbi has started Marmoush in every game since his loan move from City, most recently through Wednesday's Carabao Cup tie, and Marmoush himself said this week the squad are 'working hard' to end their goalless run - his role is not in question even though the goals are not yet coming.

sources.title: 'All of us are working hard on that' - Marmoush on fixing goalless league start

players.name: Strand Larsen
players.verdict: Undisputed starting striker with Mateta still out
players.note: Strand Larsen scored his first Premier League goal of the season against Ipswich, and Pierre Sage named the same starting side for tonight's Europa League opener against Lech Poznan, with Mateta still unavailable and Nketiah only fit enough for the bench.

sources.title: Sage: It was a hard way to lose the game

players.name: Haaland
players.verdict: Rested for tonight's Cup tie, pencilled in for Sunderland
players.note: Man City's own team news confirms Haaland was left out entirely for tonight's Carabao Cup tie with Norwich as pure squad rotation after Sunday's derby, with Maresca's own briefing pointing to him returning for Sunday's league game at home to Sunderland.

sources.title: Maresca provides injury update and team news ahead of Canaries clash

runs.note: No change, ~1.5 hours after this morning's deep pass, with tomorrow's 17:30 UTC deadline now under a day away. Fresh club-by-club sweep (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Brighton, Hull, Tottenham, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest) plus the Premier League's own injury tracker (updated today) found nothing to move any of the 15 verdicts: Arsenal's own site still has only Saliba out and no fresh word on Raya; Crystal Palace's own coverage reconfirms Mateta out until after the international break with Strand Larsen leading the line, Sarr and Nketiah also doubtful; Leeds have Gruev, Gudmundsson and Gnonto working back into training with nothing on Bogle; the league's own tracker lists Spurs' absentees as Kudus, Maddison, Kulusevski, Odobert and Solanke, with neither Marmoush nor Van Hecke among them. Gvardiol and Haaland's Carabao Cup rest (already reflected here) was reconfirmed as pure rotation ahead of Sunday's Sunderland game. This board stands as final for GW5 unless something changes before the deadline.

First deep pass for GW5, run the same day GW5 waivers processed and the squad became final (deadline tomorrow 17:30 UTC). Roughly 25 searches across every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Brighton, Hull, Tottenham, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus predicted-lineup and press-conference searches for all eight GW5 fixtures touching the squad. Six of fifteen (Bogle, Vuskovic, Gvardiol, Marmoush, Strand Larsen, Haaland) clear the bar for 'start' on permitted sources; the rest are 'likely' only because no permitted outlet has yet published this weekend's confirmed team news, not because of any real doubt - most searches surfaced only predicted-XI aggregators (Sports Mole, fotmob, RotoWire, Squawka, SI.com and similar), which are not permitted sources and were discarded even where they matched what a permitted source separately confirmed. Genuine finds: Gvardiol and Haaland were both left out entirely for tonight's Carabao Cup tie with Norwich, confirmed on mancity.com as pure rotation with both expected back Sunday against Sunderland - worth flagging since a blank cup appearance could otherwise misread as an injury; Bogle was voted Newcastle's own Hisense Player of the Match after Monday's goal; Vuskovic scored his first Brighton goal against Leeds; and Strand Larsen kept his place for tonight's Europa League opener with Mateta still out. Ajayi's hamstring situation could not be resolved either way on a permitted source - Sky Sports' own 22 August lineup has him starting and scoring, but nothing since has been published on a permitted outlet, so he sits at 'likely' rather than 'start' pending this weekend's actual team news.
